title: Queued Phase Tracer and Prognostic Splitter: tenant-aware, latency-weighted splitting policy
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Currently our prefill/decode stage splitting often uses static heuristics that ignore short-term kernel cost variability and tenant SLOs. This leads to suboptimal phase splits: some low-latency tenants experience tail latency spikes while throughput-oriented tenants get disproportionate kernel allocations.

Goal: Implement a Queued Phase Tracer (QPT) plus a Prognostic Splitter policy that uses short-horizon kernel-cost forecasts and tenant latency budgets to make per-request splitting/hedging decisions. The policy should be pluggable into the existing arbiter and produce telemetry to validate fairness/efficiency trade-offs.

Scope: design + prototype scheduler policy, metrics instrumentation, e2e latency/throughput benchmarks, safety guardrails (fallback to current policy), and a canary rollout plan. Not in scope: quantization or per-kernel codegen changes (this ticket relies on existing kernel profiles).
acceptance_criteria: QPT collects per-request micrometrics (prefill tokens, estimated kernel time, observed kernel time) without adding >1% median latency overhead
Prognostic Splitter uses a 2s forecast window and respects per-tenant latency budgets: P95 latency for latency-tier tenants improves or is not regressed by >5% under representative load
Throughput impact under 95th percentile load is within -10% of baseline for throughput-tier tenants
Automated rollout with feature flag (runtime-scheduler.qpt.enabled) and immediate fallback to baseline policy on error
End-to-end benchmarks and a dashboard with tenant breakdowns, plus at least one customer-facing incident simulation runbook

implementation_notes:
Key components:
- Queued Phase Tracer (QPT): lightweight per-request tracer that records prefill tokens, kernel hints, timestamped kernel start/end, and tenant id.
- Forecasting module: 2s sliding window exponential smoothing weight tuned per-kernel-type.
- Prognostic Splitter policy: uses forecast + tenant latency budget to decide whether to split, hedge, or route to lower-cost kernel variant.
- Safety: sampling rate, node_util threshold, and feature-flag fallback.
Instrumentation: new metrics prefixed runtime.qpt.*, and a dashboard with per-tenant P50/P95/P99 overlaid with split-rate and kernel forecast error.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for tracer and forecast logic. 2) Integration test in kube-staging with synthetic mixed tenants (latency-tier and throughput-tier). 3) Chaos run: simulate kernel slowdowns and validate fallback. 4) Canary: enable feature flag on 1 node-pool for 48h and monitor SLOs and cost.
rollout_plan: - Feature flag off by default. - Canary enable on control plane cluster pool (2 nodes) for 24-48h. - If metrics stable, ramp to 20% of latency-tier traffic over 72h. - Full enable after 10-day observation and sign-off from runtime and SRE.
owner_notes: Follow-up items if successful: 1) Replace exponential smoother with lightweight online ML model using tenant/context features. 2) Explore coupling with kernel-selection hints to prefer quantized variants for tolerant tenants.
notes: This ticket is intentionally conservative — the goal is measurable improvements for latency-sensitive tenants without risking throughput regressions. If forecast error is high we will default to baseline policy.
